author: GamingBolt
description:
VOID/BREAKER as a whole feels like a well-oiled machine at some points, and a questionable assemblage of components that threaten to (and often do) break at others. There is a lot to appreciate, whether it's those random rooms with different scenarios (including one that Doctor Who fans will instantly recognise) or watching an entire building collapse on top of enemies.

Even the endgame isn't too shabby, though it only exposes the many problems of its gameplay and optimisation. I also wasn't too impressed with the first “Exotic” weapon you can purchase – the Revolver – and the prospect of unlocking the Flamethrower feels further and further away, given how the modifiers are balanced. Whatever you do, don't enable increased Elite spawns and Hard mode. You'll have a horrific time, especially if the module RNG isn't in your favor.
title: VOID/BREAKER 1.0 Review - Does This Shooter Surpass Returnal And Saros?

author: GamingBolt
description:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake has been a title we’ve been looking forward to ever since it was announced. Of course, we know that some of you might be diving into this game for the first time. 

Things may have improved slightly, but this game is so decidedly old-school that we decided to help make your time in the world as Link a little easier with some helpful pointers. We hope these pointers help you enjoy the game as much as we enjoyed compiling them.
title: 15 Things The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Doesn't Tell You

author: GamingBolt
description:
It feels wrong not to do it at this point. We pit Onimusha: Way of the Sword and Phantom Blade Zero against each other to see which title would manage to stab the other through the heart and emerge victorious from a battle that might seem evenly matched on the surface, but becomes decidedly one-sided when you take a closer look at what each game offers.

The combat is one part of things, albeit quite an important one, but the game that surrounds a combat system must be as compelling as its fights, giving you reasons to wield your blade to the best of your ability. Well, we’re here to test just that and decide which game manages to surge ahead of the other.
title: Phantom Blade Zero vs. Onimusha Way of the Sword - The Comparison We Had To Do
